mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at -30.7% over the last four weeks with minimal week-on-week volatility (range: 0.6 percentage points). This plateau signals exhaustion of downward momentum and precedes a rebound toward baseline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined from -32.9% to -30.7% over four weeks with decelerating rate of change
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below -30% or falls further below the current -30.7% level.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PARKS mobility (9.3% → 26.7% over four weeks) indicates growing outdoor activity tolerance and social confidence. This behavioral shift transfers to indoor retail-and-recreation venues within two weeks as confidence compounds, driving RETAIL_REC upward.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 20% in any week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS increased 17.4 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the two weeks following PARKS exceeding 20%, or PARKS reverses below 15%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved from -44.4% to -41.3% (3.1 point gain), signaling commuting recovery. When combined with stable WORKPLACES near -32%, this dual recovery of movement infrastructure and workplace presence will lift retail footfall within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 3.1 points over four weeks; WORKPLACES stable at -31% to -33%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the current 28-day mean when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show simultaneous improvement.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has improved from -4.4% to -2.4% (2 point gain), indicating relaxation of restrictions on essential-services access. This signals policy easing that will extend to retail-and-recreation venues within one week, producing immediate RETAIL_REC gains.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 1 percentage point
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 2 points from -4.4% to -2.4% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the week immediately following a 1+ point improvement in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained stable at 9.0–10.1% across four weeks, indicating consistent home-based activity. Persistent residential elevation combined with modest RETAIL_REC decline suggests substitution away from retail. This substitution will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 9% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at 9.0–10.1%; RETAIL_REC stable at -30.7% to -32.9%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above 9%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility surge (9.3% → 26.7%) reflects seasonal weather improvement or holiday period onset. This seasonal lift in outdoor activity will cannibalize indoor retail-and-recreation demand, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as consumers substitute toward parks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 26.7% at t-0w, highest level in snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while PARKS remains above 25%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined from -31.6% to -32.6% (0.9 point deterioration) over four weeks, signaling weakening workplace return. This deterioration will suppress commuting-linked retail visits, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines by more than 0.5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -31.6% at t-3w to -32.6% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days when WORKPLACES shows week-on-week deterioration.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT decline (-44.4% to -41.3%) and WORKPLACES stagnation (-31.6% to -32.6%) show asymmetric recovery: transit improving faster than workplace return. This mismatch indicates commuters are not yet returning to offices, suppressing retail footfall concentrated in workplace districts. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 1 point while WORKPLACES declines or remains flat
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 3.1 points; WORKPLACES declined 1.0 point over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show divergent recovery patterns.
